newsitem.title: CHINA: China issue rules on joint shipping agents.
newsitem.headline: China issue rules on joint shipping agents.

text.p: China has issued a set of detailed rules on forming Sino-foreign joint venture shipping agents, requiring the Chinese side to have at least a 50 percent stake, the International Business Daily said on Tuesday.
China had said earlier that it would further open its services sector to foreign investment to include the formation of Sino-foreign cargo and shipping agents.
The newspaper said the Chinese side should include at least one shipping firm or at least one domestic company conducting foreign trade of more than $50 million.
Foreign partners must be international shipping agents, and joint venture shipping firms should have minimum registered capital of $1 million, it said.
The rules have been in effect since September 9, the newspaper said, quoting the Ministry of Foreign Trade and Economic Cooperation. It gave no explanation for the delay in making the announcement.
Under the rules a foreign shipping firm will not be allowed to set up a second venture within five years of the establishment of its first venture.
Joint venture companies would be allowed to conduct cargo booking, warehousing, customs clearance, insurance and international express delivery, except private mail, the newspaper said.
